{{nihongo|'''Tagata Shrine'''|田縣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Tagata Shrine''' (たがたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Komaki|Q389537|qid=Q389537}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|ja|式内小社|simple|Shikinai Shosha|qid=Q134917287}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

It is known for the {{ill|Hōnensai|Q30924149|qid=Q30924149|lt=Hōnen Festival}} held every March. The character “縣” (agata, ken) is the {{ill|Chinese character forms|Q137673972|qid=Q137673972|lt=old form}} of “県” (and is sometimes considered a {{ill|Chinese character forms|Q137673972|qid=Q137673972|lt=variant}}), so it is also written as '''Tagata Shrine''' (田県神社).

=== Enshrined deities ===
The enshrined deities are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mitoshi-no-Kami}} (みとしのかみ) and Tamahime-no-Mikoto (たまひめのみこと), gods of abundant harvests and the prosperity of descendants. According to shrine tradition, this area was part of the estate of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oarata-no-Mikoto}}, where Mitoshi-no-Kami, a god of bountiful crops, was worshiped. Tamahime-no-Mikoto was the daughter of Oarata-no-Mikoto; after her husband’s death, she returned to her parental home, raised her children admirably as a mother, and helped her father cultivate the land. In praise of these merits, she came to be enshrined as a deity.

Within the shrine grounds, many stones shaped like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=phallic symbols}} are enshrined.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown, and it is considered a very old shrine {{citation needed|date=September 2017}}. It is a shrine based on ancient indigenous beliefs and is associated with phallic worship believed to improve {{ill|Male reproductive system|Q842083|qid=Q842083}} fortune, linking faith in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=fertility}} and {{ill|Agriculture|Q11451|qid=Q11451}}. It is identified with “Tagata Shrine of Niwa District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and with “Tagata Tenjin, Senior Third Rank” recorded in the *Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō* from the third year of {{ill|Jōji|Q1146153|qid=Q1146153}} ({{ill|1364|Q6185|qid=Q6185}}). Since the current location was formerly in {{ill|Kasugai district|Q11513576|qid=Q11513576}}, the shrine must have been relocated at a later time.

=== Hōnen Festival ===
{{main|Hōnen Festival (Tagata Shrine)}}

Every year on {{ill|March 15|Q2403|qid=Q2403}}, the {{ill|Hōnensai|Q30924149|qid=Q30924149|lt=Hōnen Festival}} is held. It is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Komaki City and is read as “Hōnensai” or “Hōnenmatsuri,” also known as the “Henoko Festival.” Men parade while carrying a {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}} bearing a large phallus called Ōowase-gata, while {{ill|Miko|Q1047139|qid=Q1047139}} carry smaller phallic objects. There is a tradition that touching them grants fertility. The Ōowase-gata measures about 60 cm in diameter and over 2 meters in length, and a new one is made each year from {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|Q917187|qid=Q917187}} and dedicated to the shrine.

This ritual symbolizes the phallus as “heaven” and the vulva as “earth,” praying that “through blessings from heaven, the land is nourished, resulting in abundant harvests and fertility.” The reason it is held in spring is that it also signifies “the birth of new life.”

Nearby, the Hōnen Festival of {{ill|Ōagata Shrine|Q135732|qid=Q135732}} in {{ill|Inuyama, Aichi|Q503411|qid=Q503411}}—also known as the “Ososo Festival”—forms a pair with this festival; there, floats shaped like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=vulva}} are paraded.

=== Characteristics ===
As souvenirs, candies, chocolates, and {{ill|Objet d'art|Q7075109|qid=Q7075109}} shaped like phallic symbols are sold.

In recent years, it has become extremely popular with foreigners, and many foreign tourists visit.

Only on the day of the Hōnen Festival, multiple {{ill|Parking lot|Q6501349|qid=Q6501349}} are set up near the shrine.

=== Access ===
* About a 5-minute walk (approx. 200 m) from {{ill|Tagata Jinja-mae Station|Q7468612|qid=Q7468612}} on the {{ill|Meitetsu Komaki Line|Q6788786|qid=Q6788786|lt=Komaki Line}} of {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850|lt=Meitetsu}}.
